the question.

[56]+"""Two routes may not claim one local-ingress alias (OMN-17888).
[57]+
[58]+WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHY BOOT WAS THE WRONG PLACE TO FIND IT
[59]+------------------------------------------------------------
[60]+``omnibase_infra`` ``runtime_local_ingress.py`` registers one local-ingress alias per
[61]+``handler_routing`` entry, keyed on that entry's ``operation``, and refuses a second
[62]+registration of the same alias unless the two routes expose the SAME interface
[63]+(``_local_ingress_routes_equivalent`` compares, among other fields, the input model). On a
[64]+collision it raises::
[65]+
[66]+    ValueError: Duplicate local ingress route alias '<package>.<node>.<operation>'
[67]+
[68]+That raise happens at RUNTIME BOOT. On 2026-09-16 a contract change that was green through
[69]+every gate in both repositories made ``node_redeploy_deploy_effect`` declare one operation
[70]+twice with two different input models. ``omninode-runtime`` crash-looped, `:8086/ready`
[71]+refused, the compose-env lab-pass receipt FAILed on ``ready_main`` and
[72]+``health_dimensions``, and because delivery to staging is fail-closed on that receipt the
[73]+dev lane, staging delivery and both compose lanes were down for an afternoon.
[74]+
[75]+Nothing at PR time asked the question. This module asks it.
[76]+
[77]+WHAT IT CHECKS
[78]+--------------
[79]+1. **The real boot condition, not a re-derivation.** It calls
[80]+   ``discover_runtime_local_ingress_routes`` — the function the runtime itself calls at
[81]+   boot — and turns the ``ValueError`` it raises into a reported finding. A gate that
[82]+   re-implemented the alias rule could drift from the runtime; this one cannot, because it
[83]+   IS the runtime's own code.
[84]+2. **The contract-level cause, named.** The runtime error names an alias and a file twice;
[85]+   it does not say which operation or which models disagree. So the static half also reports
[86]+   any operation in one contract that is declared with more than one input model, which is
[87]+   the shape that produced the collision, with the contract, the operation and both model
[88]+   names.
[89]+
[90]+Both halves run. The first is authoritative about whether the runtime boots; the second is
[91]+what tells the author what to change.
[92]+
[93]+FAIL-CLOSED
[94]+-----------
[95]+A scan that resolves no package root, or that produces an implausibly small route table, is
[96]+a broken scan rather than a clean tree and exits 2. An empty result and a collapsed
[97]+discovery are otherwise the same output, and a gate that cannot tell them apart reports the
[98]+second as the first (rule 16).
[99]+
[100]+Run it directly::
[101]+
[102]+    uv run python -m omnimarket.validators.local_ingress_alias_collision
[103]+"""

[235]+    """Return findings, the alias count, and the number of contracts read."""
[236]+    alias_findings, alias_count = _alias_table_findings()
[237]+    scan_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "nodes"
[238]+    conflict_findings, contracts_read = _operation_input_model_conflicts(scan_root)

[243]+    """CLI entry point: 1 on a finding, 2 when the scan itself is unusable."""
